title: Sorrel Urban Mobility — Edge Deploy Jottings
body:
Context and quick summary:
- Customer: Sorrel Urban Mobility (fleet/ride-hailing). Want local edge LLM capability for driver assistance, voice summaries, and safety triage.
- Primary ask: on-prem/VPC edge nodes at regional depots (EU + US) to run Latency-sensitive gen/chat features when cellular intermittent. Must integrate with their telematics and map ingestion pipeline.
- Hard constraints: 95th pct token latency < 120ms for short-turn prompts (<=128 tokens). Offline/async mode for batch telemetry. GDPR PII redaction in-flight.

Call notes (2026-02-18) — high-level points: 
- Sorrel product lead (Anja) emphasized: resiliency > raw accuracy for pilot. If model fails, fallback to canned prompts with routing to ops.
- Ops asked for per-request provenance header (region, model-version, container-id) to correlate with their vehicle logs.
- Key integrator pain: NAT-to-VPC routing issues when we try to reach depot edge nodes from central control plane. They want minimal changes to firewall rules.
- Security: must use their HSM-backed keys for any persisted cache or embeddings; they cannot share keys off-network.

Technical requirements captured: 
- Deployment topology:
  * Edge nodes located in depot racks: 1x A100 per node initially, optional scale to 2x for QA bursts.
  * Control plane sits in their VPC (private-deploy mode) with optional Central mirror in Redwood cloud for telemetry only (no secrets).
  * Local model store on NVMe with pre-warmed quantized weights (4-bit) for the chosen model family (Llama-derivative).
- Network
  * Peering: VPC peering preferred. If not allowed, we need a tightly scoped outbound-only NAT and IP allowlist.
  * Heartbeat + capability endpoint must be over TLS w/ mTLS client certs.
- Secrets & keys
  * Embed cache encryption with their KMS (HSM). Redwood must be able to call their KMS via a delegated role (they prefer AWS KMS Grant).
- Observability
  * Local logs retained 14 days, full traces forwarded to their Splunk via syslog sink.
  * Token-level cost & latency not allowed to leave VPC in raw form — only aggregated metrics (1m buckets) can be exported.
- Safety and data handling
  * PII redaction to run as a prefilter on telemetry stream. If redaction confidence < 0.7, redact + route to offline review.

Gotchas / risks discovered during conversation: 
- Model warming: large quantized models still need a warm KV-cache to hit latency numbers. Depot nodes often power-cycle nightly; need startup warm strategies (checkpoint pre-load + prefix cache persistence).
- IO: NVMe contention with telemetry writes caused spikes in other customers — recommend throttle for incremental snapshotting.
- GPU fragility: vendor driver versions differ across depots — create a driver-version matrix and lockable AMI/container image.
- Network churn: cell-to-wifi handoffs cause short blackouts — must support graceful degrade to cached responses or partial-generation streaming.
- KMS policy complexity: their security team will not allow long-lived keys on the edge host. Plan must avoid persistent key material on disk.

Quick architecture notes / decisions to propose: 
- Use Redwood Private control-plane in their VPC with only a tiny agent running on depots that registers via mTLS. Agent pulls curated quantized weights from a private S3 endpoint (signed URLs short TTL).
- Persist KV cache encrypted with ephemeral data keys obtained via an HSM-backed KMS API per-boot. On shutdown/crash, cache is zeroed and can be rebuilt from scheduled warmers.
- Implement a "fallback policy" route: on lat > 150ms or missing model, return a canned short response and open a ticket to their ops via webhook.

Operational runbook snippets (to convert into playbook): 
- On node reboot: 1) agent starts, 2) request short-lived presigned URL for model weights (valid 5min), 3) stream weights to NVMe, 4) load quantized weights, 5) prewarm KV with most-used prefixes (from central telemetry snapshot).
- On network loss: flip to local-only read-mode; enqueue writes to local journal and backfill when connectivity returns.

Questions we left open (need follow-up):
- What exact GPU SKU are depots committing to? A100-40GB vs A10G will materially change batch KPS. (Action: Marcus to confirm by 2026-02-23)
- Can Sorrel accept short-lived presigned S3 URLs originating from Redwood? Their security asked for signed requests originating inside their VPC only.
- Policy for model version pinning vs auto-updates. They prefer pinning but want an ops path for quick patching. Need to propose rollout plan.

Immediate next steps / actions: 
- Action: Setup an infra discovery call (Marcus + Sorrel infra lead) — aim for 2026-02-24.
- Action: Draft driver/AMI compatibility matrix and a lockfile proposal (Elena) — due 2026-02-26.
- Action: Security deep-dive with their SecOps on KMS/HSM flows (Priya + Aisha) — schedule this week.
- Action: Prototype the agent boot sequence (minimal) and validate presigned URL flow in a lab depot (test rig ID: TR-17). Marcus to spin up.

Notes-to-self (rambling):
- Consider adding a tiny local LRU prefix cache that survives soft reboot using encrypted swap on NVMe — tradeoff: complexity vs warm-time.
- Could we offer a tiny "edge bundle" that includes a hardened kernel + tuned I/O scheduler? Might avoid a lot of depot-specific fiddling. Worth pricing.
- Evaluate 3rd-party network appliances used by depots (Cradlepoint) — NAT behavior will determine our heartbeat design.

Tentative priorities for pilot (MVP):
1) Stable single-node inference with quantized model + prewarm (verify 95% latency SLO).
2) Basic provenance headers + aggregated metrics export.
3) KMS integration for ephemeral keys + encrypted cache.
4) Fallback canned responses + webhook ops alerting.

End of notes. Rough, messy — put into a nicer playbook after infra call.
